blocks.content: Plants evolve structural features to survive environmental stress.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Xerophytes develop thick leaves, waxy coatings, reduced leaf areas, and deep roots to survive dry conditions.
Hydrophytes possess spongy tissues for buoyancy and have reduced root systems.
Mesophytes require a moderate amount of water for growth.
Halophytes are salt-tolerant plants adapted to mangrove environments.
Epiphytes rely on other trees as structural support to access direct sunlight.

blocks.content: Plants evolve structural features to survive environmental stress.
• Xerophytes – thick leaves, waxy coating, reduced leaf area, deep roots.

rows: Thick leaves, waxy coating, reduced leaf area, deep roots

blocks.content: • Hydrophytes – spongy tissues for buoyancy; reduced roots.

items: Differentiate root adaptations: Xerophytes have deep roots for water extraction, whereas Hydrophytes have reduced roots.
Halophytes are uniquely categorized by their salt tolerance in mangrove habitats.
Epiphytes grow on other trees for sunlight access rather than pulling water from host plants.

blocks.content: • Halophytes – salt-tolerant plants found in mangroves.
• Epiphytes – grow on trees to access sunlight.
